about: THE CHAIN house_new_ship (Design/content/CHAINS.md; the page is Design/content/chains/house_new_ship.md): a bigger ship built over a winter at Dorestad's dam heads. Oak bought standing in the king's wood across the river from Colonia and rafted down, rivets of heath iron from Daventre, a sail woven by the terp women of Wijnaldum, a wright who will not be hurried, a Dane with an opinion, the count at the slip, and the launching. Fourteen cards, five endings (flags ch_house_new_ship_end_keel, ch_house_new_ship_end_patched, ch_house_new_ship_end_dane, ch_house_new_ship_end_river, ch_house_new_ship_end_count) and a late epilogue (the ship on Dorestad's penny, 812-818). Cast (Design/content/spine.json): the count is cast.folcbert in his years, the moneyer cast.sigimar, the bidder for the sail cast.thiadbod (not named in the words), the Northman of the crew cast.crew.ravn (one line, not named); every other person is an ordinary invented person whom the forge names. Cards with weight 0 come only when another card schedules them; their 'when' says when they belong. Waits are flags that lapse (ch_house_new_ship_frost, _strakes, _iron_wait, _planking, _slip) and schedules. Every option's 'note' names its outcome text (chain_house_new_ship.<card>.out_<option>), which the engine does not show yet (see 'needs' in the page). Words: Data/writing/chain_house_new_ship.json. A draft for the user to overwrite.

cards.note: Step 1, the start: Dorestad, July to November, before 833, once the house has called there twice and has a pound of pennies aboard. The fixed shipwright of Dorestad (invented; the forge names him). Sources: a ship was ordered and built in the open over a winter, the buyer finding timber, iron and sail (Data/story/town_actions_793.json build_ship: ordered by Martinmas, afloat by Easter; 2,700 d new for the 6-tonne sea trader, a third down). The ship: the keeled clinker sea trader of 13 to 15 m, class north_sea_merchant_ship (Design/content/ships.md 4.10, 7.2: 12 to 15 oaks, 90 to 100 kg of iron, a sail of about 50 m2, ten men and a winter: derived from the measured replicas). Dorestad's own sea-going find is such a ship: riveted clinker, wool in her seams, wood felled after about 739 (mass.cultureelerfgoed.nl/dorestad-shipfragment; Brouwers, Jansma and Manders 2015). The beach at the dam heads had ship nails and a taken-apart clinker hull (Design/content/dossiers/dorestad.md 2). The keel's length in feet and the notched stick are invented.

cards.note: Step 2: Colonia, any call after the order. The steward of the king's estate in the old fort across the river (Deutz, a royal estate: Design/content/dossiers/colonia.md 1), invented. Sources: ship timber in the delta before about 850 is oak from the German Rhineland, and many hulls were built upstream (Brouwers, Jansma and Manders 2015, in Design/content/ships.md 2.1). The king's woods kept and his clearings cleared: Capitulare de villis c. 36 (about 800; the chapter number from memory (?)). Felling between the fifteenth and the twenty-second day of the moon, and from after midsummer to the first of January: Vegetius, Epitoma rei militaris IV.35-36 (thelatinlibrary.com/vegetius4.html, read 4 Oct 2026; our rendering); that a steward had heard of the book is invented. Rafting: Bede has timber brought down the Tyne on rafts about 721 (ship_classes_793.json, raft); a raft on the Rhine in the 790s is likely and not recorded (?). Six days down: dossiers/colonia.md (3 to 5 days by boat). The men away in Saxony: the Saxon war ends in 804. The one great trunk is the river road (step 13): a logboat widened and raised with planks, the forerunner of the Utrecht type (Vleuten 1, felled after about 734: ships.md 2.1, 4.6). Prices are the game's: 280 d for fourteen oaks and the crooks is a guess (?).

cards.note: Step 3: Dorestad, when the raft is in (scheduled by step 2: 25, 50 or 65 days). The wright sorts the timber and lays the keel. Sources: planks cleft from the trunk with wedges and hewn with the axe, not sawn, and worked green (the Roskilde builds: Design/content/ships.md 7.1, radially cleft planks; town_actions_793.json build_ship). The old keel ship at the north dams is the find of 1973-74 in the northern harbour (Hoogstraat II): four strakes 24 to 27 cm wide and a floor timber, wood felled after about 739, iron rivets, sheep's wool in the seams; she seems to have sunk there (mass.cultureelerfgoed.nl/dorestad-shipfragment, read 4 Oct 2026). That she still lay there in the 790s, and that her knees could be lifted, is the game's own (?). Old ship timber was used again: Skuldelev 5 (LATER; ships.md 7.3). Taking her floors sets changed_dorestad_old_keel: the diggers of 1973 find less.

cards.note: Step 4 (in any order with steps 2, 5 and 6): Daventre, any call after the order. The smith of the IJssel bank, invented. Sources: iron was smelted on the Veluwe, west of the IJssel, from the brown iron stones of the heath, with charcoal; the Veluwe's furnaces were among the biggest of the age (goods_793.json bar_iron; dossiers/dorestad.md 4: Veluwe iron at Dorestad; nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veluwe on the charcoal and the cut woods, read 4 Oct 2026). That the stones are the hollow 'rattle stones' and the heath's name then are from memory (?). The count of rivets: about 100 kg of iron at 50 g a rivet with its rove (ships.md 7.2, derived): two thousand. The emperor's order for ships, 810-811: chronicle_793.json 810-fleet-ordered-810 (Annales regni Francorum 811; Einhard, Vita Karoli 17). Ten kegs at 13 d against the table's 16 d a keg (goods_793.json rivets).

cards.note: Step 5 (in any order with steps 2 and 4): Wijnaldum, any call after the order. The woman who speaks for the weavers of the terp, invented. Sources: sunken huts with loom weights and spindle whorls on the terp until about 850; sheep the commonest bones (2,881); women spinning and weaving (Design/content/dossiers/wijnaldum.md 2, 3). The law prices the hand of a woman who weaves 'fresum' a quarter higher, like a harper's and a goldsmith's, and sets death or ransom on breaking into a weaving hut (Lex Frisionum, Additio sapientum: dossiers/wijnaldum.md, dossiers/doccinga.md). No servile work on the Lord's day, and for women no weaving, sewing, carding or shearing: Admonitio generalis 789 c. 81 (MGH Capit. I no. 22; from memory, not opened (?)). A sail: about 1.1 kg of wool and 100 to 130 hours of work the square metre, so fifty square metres is four women and a winter (ships.md 7.1-7.2, from the sails of Roar Ege and Ottar; Bender Jorgensen 2012). That a sail was sewn of narrow lengths, and of the long outer wool, is the replica makers' finding (?). The mound coast wants timber, grain, wine, querns, pots and iron (dossiers/doccinga.md 4). Cloak-cloth: the Frisian cloaks (goods_793.json frisian_cloth).

cards.note: Step 7: Dorestad, twenty or thirty days after the keel (flag ch_house_new_ship_frost lapsed). The turn: which ship she is to be. The Dane is a hand off a Ripa ship wintering at the dam heads, invented, and the first actor so that the riddle comes from him. Sources: King Alfred's long ships of 896 were 'shapen neither like the Frisian nor the Danish' (Anglo-Saxon Chronicle 897, tr. Giles 1847), so two patterns were known; iron rivets of the northern kind lie in the Frisian terps from 400 to 800, and Dorestad's own find is of that build (ships.md 1, 2.1); the Norse all-round ship of about 800 is lighter, lower and rowed by many (ship_classes_793.json norse_allround_ship: 16 oars, 12 men, 4 t; north_sea_merchant_ship: 4 oars, 5 men, 6 t). Godfred at Sliesthorp with his fleet, 804, and the war that follows to 810: chronicle_793.json (Annales regni Francorum 804-810). Trade between Ripa and Dorestad is in the finds; a Danish hand wintering at Dorestad is likely and not recorded (?). The line about the house's own Northman (cast.crew.ravn) shows only when the game models tongues aboard. The riddle is Gestumblindi's of the anchor (riddles_793.json r-gest-06).

cards.note: Step 8: Dorestad, twenty-five days after step 7 (flag ch_house_new_ship_strakes lapsed), and only when ten kegs of rivets are aboard or sixty days have gone without them (flag ch_house_new_ship_iron_wait lapsed). The wright will not be hurried. Sources: green oak is worked fresh and moves as it dries (the Roskilde builds: ships.md 7.1, 7.3); a 14 m trader is ten men and a winter (ships.md 7.2, derived), 150 days from order to launch (town_actions_793.json build_ship). No servile work on the Lord's day: no building, no felling (Admonitio generalis 789 c. 81, MGH Capit. I no. 22; from memory (?)); the Frisians' law fines a free man four solidi for it, twelve beyond the Lauwers (Lex Frisionum, tit. XVIII De die dominico; from memory, not opened (?)); the game's fine is 12 d. Old rivets cut out of old planks: the breaking beach at the dam heads (dossiers/dorestad.md 2); modern iron rivets need replacing after about fifteen years (ships.md 7.3, the Roar Ege). His own pace: 90 days to the launch; four more men: 60; pressed: 30 and a flawed hull.

cards.note: Step 9: Dorestad, ten or fifteen days after step 8 (flag ch_house_new_ship_planking lapsed). The count is cast.folcbert in his years ('calls every Frisian shipman': spine.md), then whoever holds the office. The second turn, and one ending: the ship given for the king's service. Sources: royal boats hauled overland and by river into Saxony (Annales Guelferbytani 797; chronicle_793.json 797-summer-ships-into-saxony, 793-12-25-wurzburg-christmas); a fleet and guards set on the coast in March 800 (Annales regni Francorum 800; chronicle 800-03-channel-coastguard); ships to be made ready on the coasts, 802 (MGH Capit. I no. 34 c. 13); 'the ships ordered to be built', 808 (MGH Capit. I no. 51 c. 9-10); the fleet ordered built on the rivers in 810 and seen by the emperor at Boulogne and Ghent in 811 (Annales regni Francorum 811; Einhard, Vita Karoli 17; chronicle 810-fleet-ordered-810). That a count took a merchant's new hull, or was given one, is invented; no count of Dorestad is named. 'carry_debt' sets the spine's db_extension (thread counts_day: a delay for a service, once for each creditor). The price of the gift: the outlay counted back (900 d), a plot at the dam heads and the count's protection.

cards.note: Step 10, ENDING keel (what the finds show): Dorestad, when the wright's time is out (flag ch_house_new_ship_slip lapsed), the count has been (step 9), the pattern is the wright's (7a) and nothing was skimped or it has been put right. The priest of the upper church (Upkirika, given to Saint Martin's in 777: dossiers/noviomagus.md) is the first actor, so the tablet comes from him. Sources: boats are launched in spring and hauled out in autumn (ships.md 7.3); a hull of green oak 'takes up' as it swells (the replica builders' experience (?)); a blessing of a ship that names Noah's ark stands in the mass-books of the age (the 'Benedictio navis' of the Romano-German pontifical of about 950, and, it is said, of the Frankish books of the 790s; not opened (?); our rendering). The schoolmaster's riddle is Symphosius 13, Navis: 'Longa feror velox formosae filia silvae' (texts_793.json symphosius_13_navis, Riese 1894; our rendering in the line). Rollers under a keel: Old Norse hlunnr, a later word (LATER) (?). The hard road (option full: good oak, new iron, the terp sail, his own pace, and the wright at least friendly) pays a second grand reward: the slip on the house's dam (unlock_work_dorestad_slip). Tar is wanted in the delta (goods_793.json tar).

cards.note: Step 11, ENDING patched: Dorestad, when the time is out and the hull is flawed (dry oak, twisted oak, old iron, a cloak-cloth sail or a hurried build), on the wright's pattern. She is launched as she is, or the wright is given a month and silver to put it right, after which step 10 comes. Sources: Skuldelev 3 was mended several times in twenty or thirty years with short lengths of plank let in below the water; the Roar Ege took a quarter of her timber and half her rivets over again in thirty-one years (ships.md 7.3); for the game an old or poor hull leaks, is slower and wets her cargo (town_actions_793.json repair). A keel ship did sink at her post in Dorestad's northern harbour (the find of 1973-74); the failure of the launch borrows the picture and does not claim to be her.

cards.note: Step 12, ENDING dane (history changed): Dorestad, when the time is out and the Dane lined her off (7b). A Frisian wright has built a ship on the northern pattern at the dam heads, forty years before the first Northman is in Dorestad's record (the raids from 834, Rorik from 850; the digs see a Scandinavian smith there perhaps after 850: dossiers/dorestad.md 3): flag changed_dorestad_dane_yard. The Dane is the first actor, so the riddle comes from him; with a sound hull and the sail aboard he will steer her (hire) and knows the way in to Ripa (unlock_pilot_ripa). Sources as step 7; the class is ship_classes_793.json norse_allround_ship (16 oars, 12 men, 4 t). A ship of that look on a Frankish coast is taken for a raider: the king's ships stop a Frisian with Danish goods (Design/npc_text_encounters.md sample 18); flag ch_house_new_ship_danish_hull is the cost that lasts. The toll man's question, 804-810: Godfred's war (chronicle_793.json).

cards.note: Step 13, ENDING river: Colonia, a hundred days after the great oak was bought (scheduled by step 2, option trunk). The house turns to the river: no sea ship is built, and the Dorestad wright keeps the earnest and his empty winter. Actors: the steward of step 2 and the wright of the bank at Colonia (invented). Sources: the Utrecht type is a logboat widened, raised with planks and lengthened; Vleuten 1, felled after about 734, about 15 by 1.1 m, of Rhineland oak, lay by an eighth-century quay on the old Rhine; the bottom of Utrecht 1 is one oak trunk at least 14 m long, hollowed to 4 to 6 cm and spread; such hulls have no iron in them, only wooden pegs, and a small mast step forward for a tow line (ships.md 2.1, 4.6, 7.2; mass.cultureelerfgoed.nl/utrecht-1). The class is ship_classes_793.json logboat_expanded. Hauling upstream by rope from the bank 'as is customary', and the Frisian skippers who passed Saint Goar's cell without the prayer: Wandalbert of Prum, Miracula sancti Goaris (839; LATER, of earlier years: dossiers/mogontia.md). No new toll where ropes are stretched: Thionville 805 (chronicle_793.json 805-12-thionville-tolls), so the line about rope-tolls is gated to 806 and after. The estate's wine goes down at Martinmas (dossiers/colonia.md 4). The steward's order is for Frisian cloaks, which the Rhineland wants (goods_793.json frisian_cloth).

cards.note: Step 14, the epilogue, years after: Dorestad, 812 to 818, for a house that launched a sea ship in this chain. The moneyer is cast.sigimar in his years. Sources: the pennies of Dorestad and Quentovic carry a ship in 812-818, with DORESTADO or DORESTATVS (dossiers/dorestad.md 4; ship_classes_793.json north_sea_merchant_ship evidence: 'a ship with a mast'); before the reform of 793-794 Dorestad's light penny carried an axe (dossiers/dorestad.md 4). That the die-cutter drew a ship lying at the dam heads, and whose, is invented. The reward is an heirloom the house keeps (unlock_heirloom_ship_penny).
